descriptionChirho: The breast or chest as a body part, used in sacrificial contexts for the wave offering breast of an animal (Exod 29:26-27; Lev 7:30-34; 8:29; 10:14-15; Num 6:20; 18:18) and in a simile for physical appearance (Dan 2:32). All three clusters denote the same anatomical referent in different grammatical forms: singular with article/construct 'the breast / breast-of' (arb: الصَّدْرَ / صَدْرَ, kor: 가슴을, swa: kidari), plural 'the breasts' (arb: الصُّدُورِ, spa: los pechos, hin: छातियों, swa: vidari), and prepositional-comparative 'like the breast of' (arb: كَصَدْرِ, kor: 처럼 가슴의, swa: kama kidari). The singular-plural distinction is inflectional, not semantic.
